titulo: Reduced Relatives, Participle Clauses and Nominalisation
descripcion: At C2 this compression is calibrated to genre: a legal or scientific register tolerates near-total nominalisation, while even sophisticated journalism keeps a verbal backbone. The C1 skill was producing the compression correctly; C2 is judging how much a given text can bear.

cuadroReferencia.titulo: How much compression a genre bears
filas: The party having failed to comply, termination follows.
Samples collected in situ were analysed off-site.
Having lost the vote, the minister resigned the next day.

ejemplos.texto: The party having failed to comply, termination follows automatically.
Having lost the vote decisively, the minister resigned the following day.
Exhausted, she said nothing for the rest of the journey.

notas: An absolute construction (the party having failed…) is essentially confined to legal and highly formal registers; using it in ordinary prose reads as an affectation.
The same participle clause that sounds efficient in a report can sound cold in narrative, where a fuller clause carries more feeling.
Judging the ceiling of compression a text can bear is itself the C2 skill — the individual constructions were already available at C1.

es.en: Spanish legal and scientific writing tends to stay more verbal than its English equivalent. Spanish speakers at C2 therefore tend to underestimate how much compression English expects in a legal or technical register, and to overestimate it in narrative.
es.es: El español jurídico y científico tiende a ser más verbal que su equivalente inglés. Por eso, los hispanohablantes de C2 suelen subestimar cuánto grado de compresión espera el inglés en registros jurídicos o técnicos y sobreestimarlo en narrativa.

de.en: German legal, technical and administrative writing is even more nominal than its English equivalent. German speakers therefore handle the dense end of the scale easily but tend to over-compress in genres such as journalism or business writing, where English keeps a clearly verbal backbone.
de.de: Deutsche juristische, technische und administrative Texte sind sogar nominaler als ihre englischen Entsprechungen. Deutschsprachige beherrschen daher das dichte Ende der Skala gut, neigen aber in Journalismus oder Geschäftssprache zur Überverdichtung, wo Englisch ein klareres verbales Rückgrat bevorzugt.

it.en: Italian bureaucratic style («burocratese») is highly nominal, so Italian speakers can produce heavy compression easily. The risk is transferring that tone to business and journalistic English, where it reads as stiff; the C2 skill is recognising how verbal those English genres remain.
it.it: Lo stile burocratico italiano («burocratese») è fortemente nominale, quindi gli italofoni sanno produrre facilmente una forte compressione. Il rischio è trasferire quel tono all'inglese commerciale o giornalistico, dove suona rigido; la competenza C2 consiste nel riconoscere quanto quei generi inglesi rimangano verbali.

fr.en: Formal French is strongly nominal («la mise en œuvre de»…), and the French press is more nominal than the English press. French speakers therefore handle legal and technical compression well but tend to over-compress journalistic or business English.
fr.fr: Le français formel est fortement nominal («la mise en œuvre de…»), et la presse française est plus nominale que la presse anglaise. Les francophones gèrent donc bien la compression juridique et technique, mais ont tendance à sur-comprimer l'anglais journalistique ou professionnel.

pt.en: Portuguese can keep almost any text verbal thanks to the personal infinitive, and tends to do so even in formal registers. Portuguese speakers therefore tend to under-compress legal and technical English, where English expects dense nominalisation.
pt.pt: O português consegue manter quase qualquer texto verbal graças ao infinitivo pessoal e tende a fazer isso até em registros formais. Falantes de português, portanto, tendem a comprimir pouco o inglês jurídico e técnico, onde o inglês espera nominalização densa.

errores: Using an absolute construction outside legal or highly formal writing, where it reads as pretentious.
Under-compressing a legal or scientific text relative to what the genre expects.
Over-compressing literary narrative, which drains it of feeling.

es: «*a efectos de*» rendered as *to effects of* instead of *for the purposes of*.
de: «*seitens*» rendered as *on the side of* instead of *on the part of* or simply *by*.
it: «*ai fini di*» rendered as *to the ends of* instead of *for the purposes of*.
fr: «*aux fins de*» rendered as *to the ends of* instead of *for the purposes of*.
pt: «*para efeitos de*» rendered as *for effects of* instead of *for the purposes of*.

mision.consigna: Write the background section of an urban planning report on rootless neighbourhoods.
requisitos: an absolute construction and two participle clauses
nominalisation calibrated to a planning report, not a legal text
one sentence you decompressed because the density hurt it
use *urban planning*, *anonymity* and *to put down roots*

microtareas.texto: Compress five sentences about *a sense of community* into two.
Decompress the densest one for a public leaflet.
Record 2 minutes on feeling *rootless*. Speech keeps its verbs.

autochequeo: Does the level of compression match the genre's actual tolerance, not just what's grammatically possible?
Is an absolute construction reserved for legal or very formal contexts?
Does literary narrative keep enough verbal texture to carry feeling?
Would an expert reader of this genre find the density normal, not either sparse or overwrought?
Have I identified the genre before judging the density?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on whether the level of nominal and participial compression matches the genre. Flag any absolute construction outside legal or very formal writing. Do not rewrite the text.
